basic_drinking_water_2024.indicator: Population using at least basic drinking water services, Indonesia (%)
basic_drinking_water_2024.source: WHO/UNICEF JMP via World Bank WDI (SH.H2O.BASW.ZS), retrieved 23 Nov 2026.

bps_2024.indicator: Households with access to improved drinking water, Indonesia (%)
bps_2024.source: Badan Pusat Statistik (BPS), Indikator Kesejahteraan Rakyat 2024, via GoodStats.

contamination.fact: Nearly 70 per cent of around 20,000 household drinking-water sources tested in a 2020 Ministry of Health study were contaminated by faecal waste.
contamination.source: UNICEF Indonesia, 7 Feb 2022, citing the Ministry of Health household drinking-water quality study (2020).

improved_drinking_water_trend.indicator: Households with access to improved drinking water, Indonesia (%)
improved_drinking_water_trend.note: Definition changed between 2019 and 2020 (from 'improved drinking-water source' to 'improved drinking water'); the series should be read with care across that break.
improved_drinking_water_trend.source: Profil Kesehatan Indonesia (Kementerian Kesehatan RI), compiled by ARC Institute — Health Profile Atlas, indicator ENV-01-096.

safely_managed.indicator: Population using safely managed drinking water services, Indonesia (%) — SDG 6.1.1
safely_managed.source: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP), via World Bank World Development Indicators (SH.H2O.SMDW.ZS), retrieved 23 Nov 2026.

sanitation.indicator_basic: Population using at least basic sanitation services, Indonesia (%)
sanitation.source_basic: WHO/UNICEF JMP via World Bank WDI (SH.STA.BASS.ZS), retrieved 23 Nov 2026.
sanitation.source_open_defecation: WHO/UNICEF JMP via World Bank WDI (SH.STA.ODFC.ZS), retrieved 23 Nov 2026.

targets_2030.sdg_6_1: By 2030, achieve universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water for all.
targets_2030.sdg_6_2: By 2030, achieve access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene for all and end open defecation.
